clue.text: Gasps for breath in schoolboy togs

explanation.surface: A breathless schoolboy panting in his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: One reading is breath coming in short pants (gasps); the other is the short trousers schoolboys once wore. 'Togs' is slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasping breaths are short pants of air, and short trousers were the standard dress of young schoolboys.

clue.text: Straighten robes, like a judge

indicators.note: to straighten something untidy is to rearrange it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A judge tidies his gown before court.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'as sober as a judge' makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as sober as a judge' links calm, temperate seriousness with the bench.

clue.text: Ring the phone, perhaps, on French island for the wine man

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word phone in some other order

parts.note: île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: Calling a wine expert on an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PHONE into ENOPH, which sits between O and ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur or lover of wine is the man in question, from Greek oinos for wine.

clue.text: Novel way to drive the point home

definitions.text: way to drive the point home

explanation.surface: An inventive method for making an argument hit home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turn of the Screw is Henry James's ghost novella; a screw's point is driven in by turning it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James wrote the ghostly tale of that title, and twisting is how a screw is forced into wood.

clue.text: Don't do anything to the tar mark

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
a stain is a mark left on something

explanation.surface: Advice to leave a tarry smudge alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the sticky stuff, but it is the old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain, holding back from acting or voting, is to do nothing.

clue.text: Heavy weight on a posh car's back seats

parts.note: a tonne is a metric weight of a thousand kilograms
U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: Something heavy dropped on the rear of a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a positional link: the weight sits before A and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear passenger compartment of an open motor car was called by this French term for a cask.

clue.text: Competent as third man, say

indicators.note: say tells us the name is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, was the third human in Genesis

explanation.surface: A cricketer judged good enough to field at third man.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man looks like a cricket fielding position (behind the batsman on the off side); here it is Abel, after Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable or skilled is to be competent.

clue.text: Snapped railway trains satisfactorily, first in Euston

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railway trains
OK means all right or satisfactorily

indicators.note: first in tells us to take the opening letter of Euston

explanation.surface: A photographer took pictures of trains running well at Euston station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapped' suggests photographs; it means broken. Euston is a London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has cracked in two has broken apart, which is what snapped means.

clue.text: Tate venue's poor turn out

indicators.note: poor suggests these words are in a bad state and must be reworked

parts.note: the 's reads as 'is', a link, so only venue gives letters

explanation.surface: An art gallery's location has drawn a disappointing crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' looks like a noun for attendance; it is the verb meaning result. The Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is to happen in the end, to result.

clue.text: Flight time of Milton's angels a surprise, but soon over

explanation.surface: Fallen angels in Paradise Lost, and a short-lived sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: In Paradise Lost the rebel angels fall from Heaven for nine days, a flight of that length.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's rebels fell through chaos for that period, and the phrase also names a brief sensation quickly forgotten.

clue.text: Mountain god, holy in india

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for mountain, as in Ben Nevis
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A mountain deity revered as sacred in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is elliptical: 'holy [city] in India', now Varanasi on the Ganges.
explanation.definitionFit: This old name for Varanasi denotes the Hindu pilgrimage city on the Ganges, sacred to millions.

clue.text: To have a row about a decoration is offensive

indicators.note: about puts the row round the decoration, enclosing it

parts.note: a row is a loud din, a noise
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Squabbling over a medal is distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' could be a line, but here it is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foul-smelling or disagreeable is offensive.

clue.text: One who is unprincipled about testamentary proof

parts.note: re means concerning or about
probate is the legal proving of a will

explanation.surface: A dishonest person meddling with the proving of a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel without morals is an unprincipled person.

clue.text: Construct perpendicular

explanation.surface: Building something upright.
explanation.definitionFit: To build is to put up, and something standing straight up is upright.

clue.text: Long leg gets the bird

explanation.surface: A long-legged wader gets its name.
explanation.walkthrough: A stilt is a pole for walking high, a long artificial leg, and also a long-legged wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pole used to walk raised up acts as a long leg, and a wader of that name shares it.

clue.text: Is hauled up for a warning when things start getting rough

definitions.text: Is hauled up for a warning when things start getting rough

parts.words: Is hauled up for a warning when things start getting rough
parts.note: describes the canvas signal hoisted at coastguard stations when a gale is expected

explanation.surface: A signal raised as the weather turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped signal was hoisted on a mast to warn sailors of gales.

clue.text: Kind of real gun to get one a pain in the head

indicators.note: kind of hints the words are a variant, rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A real gun that gives one a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' rearranges REALGUN into NEURALG, then I and A follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is nerve pain, often a stabbing ache in the face or head.

clue.text: Old man who puts the bells in order

definitions.text: who puts the bells in order

explanation.surface: An elderly bell-ringer arranging the peal.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandsire is also a well-known method in English change-ringing, an order for ringing the bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is an old man, and Grandsire is a change-ringing method setting the sequence of bells.

clue.text: Go in first over, with no fixed boundary

parts.note: in cricket, the first batsmen in are said to open
ended means finished, over

explanation.surface: A batsman goes in first in an over with nothing to stop the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: To open the batting in cricket is to go in first; 'over' and 'boundary' add cricket colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestricted, with no set limit or conclusion.

clue.text: Does the family make gloves? Yes

definitions.text: Does the family make gloves? Yes

parts.note: female deer are does
one's kin is one's family

explanation.surface: A question about a family firm of glovers, firmly answered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: does plus kin really do make gloves, as doeskin is soft glove leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is the soft hide of a female deer, used for fine gloves.

clue.text: Girl expresses annoyance, having to come into the open

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a girl entering society
ouch is a cry of pain or irritation

explanation.surface: A girl complains about having to go outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' is a link joining wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To debouch is to emerge from a narrow place into open ground, as troops or a river do.

clue.text: A form of jelly

explanation.surface: A wobbly dessert in a mould.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shape' was an old word for a jelly or blancmange set in a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is an outline or figure, and a moulded jelly pudding was once called by the same word.

clue.text: Ape caught on double motorway

indicators.note: double tells us to write the motorway letters twice

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A monkey seized on a dual carriageway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy them, imitate their manner.

clue.text: The civil habits of Jerusalem, maybe

explanation.surface: Everyday dress worn in the Holy City.
explanation.walkthrough: Mufti is civilian clothes worn by someone who usually wears uniform; the Grand Mufti of Jerusalem is a senior Islamic jurist.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain clothes worn off duty go by this name, as does a Muslim legal scholar such as the one at Jerusalem.

clue.text: Decorate the bride more creatively

indicators.note: creatively suggests the letters are rearranged in an inventive new order

explanation.surface: Dressing up a bride with extra flair.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish with stitched ornament or added detail is to decorate.

clue.text: Storms that put an end to the ' sale of peerages

indicators.note: the end portion of the word peerages holds the letters
the end portion of the word peerages holds the letters

explanation.surface: Fury that stopped the selling of titles.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the end of 'peerages'; the sale of honours was a 1920s scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Storms of anger are furies, outbursts of temper.

clue.text: Stout Cortez out of position at a slack time?

explanation.surface: An explorer from a famous poem has lost his footing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Keats's sonnet stout Cortez stood 'upon a peak in Darien'; out of position, he is off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's Cortez dislodged from his mountain top is off it, and quiet low-demand hours are described with the same phrase.

clue.text: The sun was Icarus's

parts.note: in myth the sun melted the wax of his wings, causing his fall and ruin

explanation.surface: The myth of the boy who flew too high.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin or downfall: the sun brought about his destruction.

clue.text: Heard rhyme about this prince

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the spoken spelling round
heard signals that the word is spoken, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: the word rhyme, said aloud

explanation.surface: A ruler hears a poem written about him.
explanation.walkthrough: RIME, the old spelling as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner, sounds like rhyme; 'about' turns it to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab ruler or commander bears this title of prince.

clue.text: In such an unsecured state the Crown can't afford gambling

explanation.surface: The Treasury cannot afford a betting habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown and Anchor is a dice gambling game; 'the Crown' alone is that game with the anchor dropped, so it is anchor-less.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship with no anchor is unsecured, and Crown and Anchor shorn of its second word fits the same phrase.
